title: Two-term constant-sheaf resolution of Z/ell^N and its tensor augmentation
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $N\geq1$, and $\mathcal C$ a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $R=(\mathbf Z_\ell)_{\mathcal C}$ and $Q=(\mathbf Z/\ell^N\mathbf Z)_{\mathcal C}$ be constant sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], with the coefficient rings of [def-weil-l-adic-numbers]. Use sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], cochain complexes and quasi-isomorphisms [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules, def-pc-quasi-iso-modules], and total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. The complex $C=[R\xrightarrow{\ell^N}R]$, in degrees $-1,0$, has flat terms [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex], and its degree-zero quotient augmentation $\epsilon:C\to Q[0]$ is a quasi-isomorphism. For any $R$-module sheaf $L$ such that multiplication by $\ell^N$ is injective, the canonical augmentation
$$\operatorname{Tot}(L[0]\otimes_R C)\longrightarrow(L\otimes_R Q)[0]$$
is a quasi-isomorphism. Here the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] canonically identifies $L\otimes_R Q$ with $L/\ell^NL$, by $x\otimes\bar a\mapsto a[x]$.

proof.text: Put $A=\mathbf Z_\ell$, $B=\mathbf Z/\ell^N\mathbf Z$, and $t=\ell^N$. The first clause of [lem-weil-pbc-standard-quotients-perfect] gives the ordinary two-term resolution $[A\xrightarrow{t}A]\to B[0]$, with the quotient augmentation. Thus $0\to A\xrightarrow{t}A\to B\to0$ is exact. Regard this as a sequence of constant presheaves of $A$-modules on $\mathcal C$: at each object it is the same exact sequence. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-r-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact], its sheafification is exact. By [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] the resulting sequence is $0\to R\xrightarrow{t}R\xrightarrow{q}Q\to0$. All maps are $R$-linear, with the action obtained by sheafifying the constant $A$-actions. In the abelian module-sheaf category of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], this says that multiplication by $t$ has zero kernel and that $q$ exhibits $Q$ as its cokernel.

source.place: Tag 03EI, lemma-sheafification-exact, applied to the constant presheaf of rings A; ordinary coefficient resolution from the cited existing node

proof.text: By [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed], $R$ is the tensor unit, so tensoring with $R$ is naturally isomorphic to the identity and is exact. Tensoring with the zero sheaf is zero: sectionwise $M(U)\otimes_{R(U)}0=0$, and its sheafification is zero by [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Thus $R$ and $0$ are flat by [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], and every term of $C$ is flat. Since $C^i=0$ for $i>0$, [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site] applies with upper bound $0$ and shows that $C$ is K-flat. Its hypotheses require only a ringed site and flat terms, both established here.

source.place: Tag 06YQ, lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat; tensor unit as in sites-modules.tex Section 03EK

proof.text: Set $\epsilon^0=q$ and $\epsilon^i=0$ for $i\ne0$. The relation $qt=0$ makes this a cochain map. The cohomology formula of [def-pc-acyclic-complex-modules] and Step 1 give $H^{-1}(C)=\ker(t:R\to R)=0$, $H^0(C)=\operatorname{coker}(t:R\to R)\cong Q$, and zero in every other degree. The degree-zero cohomology map of $\epsilon$ is exactly this cokernel identification, since it is induced by $q$. All other cohomology maps are between zero sheaves. Hence $\epsilon:C\to Q[0]$ is a quasi-isomorphism by [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules].

source.place: Tag 0115, definition-quasi-isomorphism-cochain; elementary two-term cohomology calculation

proof.text: For any $R$-module sheaf $L$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits] to the cokernel diagram $R\xrightarrow{t}R\xrightarrow{q}Q\to0$ of Step 1. This finite diagram is small in the module universe, as required, and the site is small. Tensoring with $L$ therefore identifies $L\otimes_R Q$ with the cokernel of $1_L\otimes t:L\otimes_R R\to L\otimes_R R$. Use the unit isomorphism of [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed], explicitly $x\otimes a\mapsto ax$ with inverse $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. It takes $1_L\otimes t$ to multiplication by $t$ on $L$, since $x\otimes ta\mapsto tax$. Consequently there is a unique isomorphism $\phi:L\otimes_R Q\xrightarrow{\sim}L/tL$ with $\phi(1_L\otimes q)(x\otimes a)=a[x]$. Here $L/tL$ is the cokernel in the abelian sheaf category, rather than an assumed sectionwise quotient. This formula characterizes a map of cokernels, and its inverse is the map induced by $x\mapsto x\otimes\overline1$. The two composites are identities because they agree after the respective cokernel projections. In particular, on pure tensors it is $x\otimes\bar a\mapsto a[x]$, exactly the identification in the statement. This quotient identification uses no injectivity hypothesis on $L$.

source.place: Tag 03EP, lemma-tensor-commute-colimits, item (2); Section 03EK tensor unit and the cokernel universal property

proof.text: By [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], only bidegrees $(0,-1)$ and $(0,0)$ contribute to $\operatorname{Tot}(L[0]\otimes_R C)$. Under $x\otimes a\mapsto ax$ this is $[L\xrightarrow{t}L]$ in degrees $-1,0$: the differential is $1_L\otimes t$ and the sign is $(-1)^0=1$. The canonical augmentation is $1_L\otimes\epsilon$; its degree-zero map, followed by $\phi$ of Step 4, sends $x$ to $[x]$. Now use the stated injectivity of $t:L\to L$. The cohomology formula of [def-pc-acyclic-complex-modules] gives zero in degree $-1$, $L/tL$ in degree $0$, and zero elsewhere. The augmentation induces $\phi^{-1}$ on degree-zero cohomology and the isomorphism between zero sheaves in all other degrees. It is therefore a quasi-isomorphism by [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules], proving the final clause with its specified map.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q20-57b2b5073 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all 5 steps, every cited statement, the parent lem-pur-finite-kummer-level (its step 6 uses this item) and the main-20261015 Kummer proof. In Stacks I checked 03EI (sites-modules l.874: any presheaf of rings, so it covers the constant presheaf Z_l), 03EP(2) (l.4013) and 06YQ lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat (sites-cohomology l.3120). The statement is unchanged, uses the discrete constant (Z_l)_C, and is true. Small cases: L=0, L=R with ell=2 and N=1 on the point site, L=(Q_l)_C, and torsion L for the identification all agree; L=Q shows the injectivity hypothesis is needed. Step 1 sheafifies the exact ordinary resolution and takes Mod(R) kernels and cokernels. Step 2: the unitor makes R flat, 0 is flat, and bounded-above flat implies K-flat. Step 3 (elementary): H^-1=ker t=0 and H^0=coker t=Q. Step 4: tensor preserves the finite cokernel diagram, and the unitor gives L tensor Q = L/tL by x tensor a-bar to a[x]. Step 5 (elementary): Tot is [L -t-> L] with sign +1, and the augmentation induces phi^{-1} on H^0. No new nodes, so no relabelling. The grep found no duplicate in the DAG. No SGA. I accept the four declared tool_uses: lem-weil-pbc-standard-quotients-perfect, lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed, lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site and lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits. Not a delivery fault: lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site gives source tag 06YS, but the right tag is 06YQ; that is for maintenance. No fixes.
